statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 12% after the overnight Nasdaq-100 futures high was extended a few points past the level refused twice earlier, inside a band still worth only 0.35% of index value.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window spanning the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech is the session's main checkpoint, and the published forecast reaches WATCH across both of those hours. Weekly ADP at 12:15 UTC and the August trade balance at 12:30 UTC are the nearer checkpoints, with the 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC relevant because the long end sits at 24-year highs. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ edges the overnight high to 31,418 as crude drops below $88 on a surprise Saudi price cut and the long end holds 24-year highs
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,413.25, up 95.50 points (+0.30%) from the 31,317.75 previous close, with the Globex range now 31,309.25-31,418.00. The change that matters for the Tail score is that the 31,411.25 high, refused twice during the preceding hours, has now been taken: the high printed 31,414.75 and then 31,418.00 as price pressed the boundary. That is genuine extension evidence and it is why Tail steps up from 10% to 12%. It is also small. The new high sits roughly seven points above the old one, about 0.02% of index value, and the full overnight band spans 108.75 points or 0.35% of the index. A boundary taken by a few points inside a third-of-a-percent range is a slow grind, not the persistent no-retracement path this score exists to detect, and the requirement of observed one-way structure or multiple independent current amplifiers is not met. The clearest new cross-asset development is in energy, and it runs against the geopolitical narrative. WTI has broken down to $87.68, off 1.96% on the day and sitting at the $87.63 session low against a $90.05 high, after Saudi Aramco set the official selling price differential for Arab Light into Asia at $5 below the regional benchmark, the weakest since 2020 and the opposite of the increase traders had flagged. That supply signal is outweighing continued Houthi pressure on Saudi infrastructure and the earlier rerouting of exports through Ras Tanura and the Gulf of Oman. Crude falling roughly two percent while supply-side attacks continue is a market absorbing escalation rather than repricing it, and it is disinflationary at the margin, so the energy channel subtracts from Tail. The rates picture is the live dislocation. The 10-year sits at 5.31% against a 4.83% 2-year, and the 30-year closed at 5.66%, the highest daily close of the cycle, with the long end briefly printing new multi-decade highs intraday; the MOVE index rose 5.88% to 113.61, making rates volatility the standout, and EURUSD touched a 17-month low of 1.1161 before recovering toward 1.1220. That bear-steepening combination is the main reason Stress edges to 46% and stays in the elevated band. Equity-side evidence is the opposite of stressed. VIX at 15.45 is down 0.45% in a 15.43-15.52 range, implying no demand for protection; E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,845.25 (+0.24%) sit at the top of their own 7,829.00-7,847.50 range; and Nvidia is indicated at $240.75 (+0.77%) pre-market after a $238.90 record close, keeping megacap and semiconductor tone aligned to the upside. Against that alignment, the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 5 October at a record 31,076.44 (+0.87%) but 40.92 points below its 31,117.36 session high, so even the record close faded off its extreme, and October hike pricing has collapsed to roughly 20% from about 70% a week earlier, removing a near-term policy shock. Two amplifiers are aligned, one is pointing the other way, implied volatility is compressed and the range remains narrow, so Tail stays in the low band at 12% while Stress carries the yield story.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour on 5 October, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 11% at 09:00 UTC through 14% at 10:00, dipped to 7% at 12:00, then climbed through the U.S. session to the 20% peak before decaying to 9% by 00:00 UTC on 6 October. It printed 12% at 01:00 UTC as the Globex high was first set and settled between 8% and 10% through 08:00 UTC. Stress fell from 50% to 45% as realised volatility compressed even while long-end yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 86% and 89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds at 12% through the European session, steps to 14% as weekly ADP and the trade balance approach at 12:15 and 12:30 UTC, peaks at 20% across the first two U.S. cash hours, then decays through the afternoon with a 16% reading around the 3-year auction and a secondary 17% around the cash close before easing to 10-11% across the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 45% and 54%, held up at the floor by a yield level rather than by equity volatility, and Confidence decays from 87% to 76% as the live price-path evidence behind the assessment ages.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NQ 31,413-31,415 (+0.30%) has nudged the Globex high to 31,418.00, a few points above the 31,411.25 level refused twice earlier, so the boundary is being taken rather than rejected. The advance is a slow grind inside a 0.35% band, not a no-retracement path, so Tail rises only marginally.
